lines.p1: When Claude Code explores a codebase by reading files, every file lands in the context window, and every token costs money.
lines.p2: On a big repo, most of those tokens go to code that has nothing to do with the task.
lines.g1: So index the code once with graphify. It turns your source into a knowledge graph of files, functions and how they connect.
lines.g2: Commit the graph, and the whole team shares it. Nobody pays to re-explore the same repo.
lines.g3: Now the agent queries the graph through the graphify M C P server, instead of loading the big JSON file, and reads only the few files that matter.
lines.pl1: Next, the agent queries the graph over M C P, reads your requirements, and writes an execution plan.
lines.pl2: You confirm the plan before any code changes. If something is off, it refines the plan and asks again.
lines.pl3: Fixing a plan costs a few lines. Fixing code costs a rewrite.
lines.d1: Once approved, the main agent delegates each step to a subagent.
lines.d2: Each subagent starts with a small, clean context, works on its own slice, and returns only a short summary.
lines.v1: At the end, validate: run the tests, and check the result against the requirements.
lines.v2: Anything missing goes back to a subagent for a fix.
lines.outro: Index once, plan first, delegate small, validate last.
